overview: Tanwan Inc. (formerly ZX Inc. / 中旭未來, renamed 8 August 2025) is a Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed Chinese mobile and web game publisher built around licensed legacy IPs — 'Legend' (傳奇), 'Yulgang' (熱血江湖) and 'MU' (奇蹟MU) — distributed across apps, web, and fast-growing WeChat/Douyin mini-programs in China and, increasingly, overseas under the 'Game Lovin' brand. The Group has diversified into a 'New Consumption' segment (pop toys under the TANWAN brand, including a Garfield IP license, and the 'ZAZA GRAY' fast-food brand) and has built a sizeable securities investment portfolio (Century Huatong, Moore Threads, and other AI-related equities) that increasingly drives reported earnings. Reports in RMB with a 31 December year-end.

business_model.summary: Core revenue comes from marketing/publishing third-party-developed and self-owned online games under a 'self-run' (higher revenue share, higher S&M cost) and 'joint-run' (revenue-share with platforms/co-publishers) model, monetized mainly through in-game purchases funded by heavy performance-marketing (UA) spend. A small (~2.6% of revenue) consumer products segment sells fast food and pop toys. Growth in FY2025-H1 2026 has shifted toward low-cost mini-program distribution and overseas expansion, while FY2025 and H1 2026 net income was dominated by unrealized fair-value gains on a large portfolio of listed-equity investments (Century Huatong, Moore Threads, etc.), not operating cash generation.

revenue_streams.name: Self-run game publishing
revenue_streams.trend: declining (mature IP gross billings rolling off)

revenue_streams.name: Other marketing business
revenue_streams.trend: declining (de-emphasized, e.g. online literature wound down)

business_model.customer_type: B2C mobile/web game players in China (~80% of revenue) and overseas (~20%, growing); monetization via microtransactions, not subscriptions
business_model.geographic_mix: Chinese mainland ~81%, Hong Kong/Macao/Taiwan and overseas ~19% (H1 2026); overseas revenue grew 33.6% YoY in FY2025 and 12.2% YoY in H1 2026, rising from 11.1% of revenue (FY2024) to 20.0% (FY2025)

competitive_position.market_position: Small/mid-tier niche publisher specializing in nostalgia-driven legacy IP (Legend/MU/Yulgang-style) reskins and mini-program adaptations rather than AAA original content; a long-tail player relative to Tencent/NetEase scale

moat_factors.description: Long-running rights to nostalgic, high-loyalty IPs (Legend, MU, Yulgang, and newly added Jin Yong Martial Arts/Soul Land titles) give a recognizable content pipeline, but IPs are licensed, not owned, and face renewal/royalty risk

Self-developed 'Hetu' analytics and 'Luoshu' placement systems plus AI-generated creative claim an ~80% AI ad-penetration rate and >70% efficiency gains, potentially structurally lowering user-acquisition costs

Early, successful adaptation of Legend/MU-style IPs into WeChat/Douyin mini-games (e.g., 'City of Dragontrail' topped WeChat's bestseller list) positions the company in a fast-growing (>20% YoY) mini-game sub-segment
Growing but still a minority (~19-20%) of revenue; competes against far larger global publishers in Korea/SE Asia/US/Europe

weaknesses: Reliance on licensed (not owned) legacy IPs, with core domestic titles (Legend-family) in mature/declining gross-billings phase
High customer-acquisition cost structure typical of mobile game publishing; selling & distribution expense has historically run 40-85% of revenue
Small scale versus Tencent/NetEase limits pricing power with platforms and IP licensors
Earnings increasingly disconnected from core operations due to a large, volatile securities investment book
Diversification into pop toys/fast food is unproven and unrelated to the core competency of game publishing

growth_drivers: Pipeline of new premium IP titles (Soul Land: Legend of Evil Slayer, Legend of King 2, Jin Yong Martial Arts series, Dreamscape Warrior) slated for launch through 2026
Continued mini-program game expansion riding a China mini-game market projected to exceed RMB74.5bn in 2026 (+22% YoY)
Overseas expansion via 'Game Lovin' brand into Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, Europe, Americas and the Middle East — overseas revenue growing faster than domestic
'AI + Games' initiative lowering marketing/creative production costs and supporting new content formats (AI short dramas/comics) as an emerging monetization avenue
New consumption diversification (Garfield-licensed pop toys, 200+ collaborating artists, ZAZA GRAY fast food) targeting cross-sell to the existing game-player user base

HK$468m zero-coupon convertible bond proceeds earmarked for AI-sector strategic investments (Moore Threads, Victory Giant Technology, Beijing Sanqi Wanwu/VAST), expanding the investment portfolio further
MSCI China Small Cap Index inclusion (Feb 2026) and continued share buybacks signal capital-markets profile improving, potentially supporting valuation/liquidity

business.risk: Core IP maturity / gross billings decline
business.description: FY2025 revenue fell 25.5% YoY and H1 2026 revenue fell 6.0% YoY, driven by declining gross billings from mature Legend-family and other aging titles; company explicitly describes core IP growth as 'moderated' with billings in later life-cycle stages

Business model depends on licensing arrangements with third-party IP owners (South Korean originators of Yulgang/MU) and game developers for both self-run and joint-run titles; loss or non-renewal of key licenses would directly hit revenue
Pop toy (Garfield license) and fast-food (ZAZA GRAY) businesses are small (2.6% of revenue) and outside core competency; success unproven
Management explicitly cites 'rising user acquisition costs' as an industry-wide challenge partially offset (not eliminated) by AI tooling

financial.description: FY2025 net profit of RMB1,560.2m was overwhelmingly driven by ~RMB1.9bn of other income/gains, chiefly unrealized fair-value gains on FVTPL equity holdings (Century Huatong, Moore Threads) — disclosed FVTPL fair-value asset balance grew from RMB914m (H1 2025) to RMB2,893m (FY2025) to RMB3,404m (H1 2026). In H1 2026, RMB268.4m of RMB282.6m pre-tax profit (95%) came from 'Investments at FVTPL and Others' versus only RMB14.2m from the core game and consumer-product businesses combined. These gains are unrealized, mark-to-market, and reversible; a decline in the underlying share prices (Century Huatong, Moore Threads) would materially reduce or reverse reported profit

financial.risk: Operating cash flow volatility tied to bills payable, not core cash generation
financial.description: Operating cash flow swung from -RMB468m (H1 2025) to +RMB123m (FY2025) to -RMB101m (H1 2026); these swings are primarily a function of bills-payable paydown/timing to game developers and suppliers rather than underlying operating cash burn, and should not be read as a trend in core profitability

Large single-name exposures (Century Huatong ~19.3% of total assets, Moore Threads ~17.9% of total assets as of FY2025) create concentration and mark-to-market risk; combined the two names were ~37% of total assets at FY2025-end

financial.risk: FX exposure from HK$ convertible bond
financial.description: HK$468m zero-coupon CB issued Jan 2026 introduced exchange losses in H1 2026 from HKD/USD/RMB fluctuation

regulatory.description: All new titles require National Press and Publication Administration (NPPA) publication number approval; approval pace has been accelerating in 2026 (NPPA approved 1,110+ domestic and 37+ import titles YTD through July 2026 per Niko Partners), reducing near-term bottleneck risk but policy could tighten again

PRC's 15th Five-Year Plan (issued March 2026) explicitly encourages digital culture industries including online games, a tailwind, but Chinese gaming remains subject to periodic anti-addiction, minor-protection, and content-review tightening historically (e.g., 2021 restrictions)

regulatory.risk: Cayman/HK corporate structure and cross-border capital controls
regulatory.description: Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed holding company with PRC operating subsidiaries; subject to typical offshore-listing structural and potential future ODI/cross-border capital flow scrutiny

macro.description: In-game spending is discretionary; a soft Chinese consumer environment could pressure monetization even as user numbers grow slowly (+0.82% YoY in H1 2026)

macro.risk: Equity market volatility (China A-shares / Hong Kong tech)
macro.description: Given reported earnings are now dominated by mark-to-market gains on Chinese listed equities (Century Huatong, Moore Threads — both exposed to AI/semiconductor sentiment), a broad China/HK equity market pullback would directly and significantly impair reported profit
RMB reporting currency with HKD-denominated convertible bond and multi-currency cash balances (SGD, HKD, USD, JPY, EUR) creates translation and transactional FX exposure

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China domestic gaming market revenue grew 7.68% in 2025 to RMB350.79bn and 12.17% YoY in H1 2026 to RMB188.45bn; mini-program/mini-game sub-segment growing much faster (+34.4% in 2025, projected +22%+ in 2026 to RMB74.5bn); global mobile games market ~US$108bn in 2025 (+7.7% YoY per Newzoo)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — discretionary in-game spending, but legacy nostalgia IP demand (Legend/MU-style) has proven relatively resilient across cycles in China; new consumption segment adds limited additional cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct — company carries minimal bank debt (gearing ratio 0.02 at FY2025) and a zero-coupon convertible bond; indirect sensitivity through impact on Chinese/HK equity valuations affecting its large FVTPL investment portfolio
key_input_costs: game developer co-development and revenue-sharing costs

recent_developments.event: Shareholders approved changing the company's English name from 'ZX Inc.' to 'Tanwan Inc.' and Chinese name from '中旭未來' to '貪玩', effective 8 August 2025 (HKEX stock short name changed to 'TANWAN' from 2 September 2025); rebranding explicitly aligns the listed entity with its flagship 'Tanwan Game' consumer brand
CEO transition: Ms. LIANG Wenhong resigned as CEO; Chairman Mr. WU Xubo assumed the CEO role
Signed a five-year exclusive IP licensing agreement for 'GARFIELD Family' collectible toys, part of the pop-toy diversification (TANWAN brand)
Signed a five-year Artist Work Development Cooperation Agreement with 200+ collectible artists for pop-toy/art derivative products

Announced issuance of HK$468 million zero-coupon convertible bonds due 2027, fully subscribed by LMR Multi-Strategy Master Fund Limited, earmarked for AI-sector strategic investments; completed 8 January 2026
Added to the MSCI China Small Cap Index (having already joined the Hang Seng Composite Index in March 2024)

FY2025 and H1 2026 results show a sharp divergence between reported net profit and core operating profit: FY2025 net profit of RMB1,560.2m (vs RMB44.0m in FY2024) was driven almost entirely by ~RMB1.9bn of fair-value gains on FVTPL investments (Century Huatong, Moore Threads); H1 2026 profit fell 67.2% YoY to RMB213.3m as those fair-value gains shrank, with core game/consumer-product businesses contributing only RMB14.2m of the period's RMB282.6m pre-tax profit
Continued share buybacks (16.3m shares repurchased since May 2025 for ~HK$233m at ~HK$14.30 average) and expansion into new AI-generated short-drama/comic content as an adjacent growth track
Launched new mobile title 'Space Hunter: Awakening', which topped the iOS Free List shortly after launch; 'Yulgang: Awakening' entered open beta 31 July 2026

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (issued ~March 2026) / H1 2026 Interim Report

items.notes: Management does not issue formal numerical guidance; outlook sections are qualitative, citing a 'rich and diversified pipeline' of titles (Soul Land: Legend of Evil Slayer, Legend of King 2, Blue Moon Dragon Slayer, Jin Yong Martial Arts titles, Dreamscape Warrior) poised for 'imminent release' to support growth

items.period: Achieved as of FY2025 / maintained H1 2026
items.notes: Operational KPI target/achievement cited consistently across FY2025 annual and H1 2026 interim reports, not a forward target per se but a stated current capability level

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman/CEO Wu Xubo's letters emphasize 'long-termism,' continued investment in classic IP rejuvenation, mini-program and overseas expansion, and full integration of AI across publishing, marketing and R&D. Management explicitly flags that 'Legend' core products have 'entered a mature operational phase' with 'moderated' gross billings growth, and that H1 2026 profit decline was 'primarily due to' lower FVTPL fair-value gains and continued decline in domestic game gross billings — an unusually direct acknowledgment that reported profit is not a clean read of operating momentum.

bull_case: Deep, multi-decade nostalgia IP catalog (Legend, MU, Yulgang) generates durable, high-loyalty, high-ARPU player bases with proven ability to monetize across new formats (mini-programs, overseas markets)
Fast-growing mini-program game and overseas distribution channels are genuinely offsetting domestic legacy-title decline with higher-margin, lower-cost-of-acquisition growth
AI-driven marketing/creative tooling (Hetu/Luoshu systems) is a real, quantified (70%+ efficiency gain) structural cost advantage versus smaller peers lacking such infrastructure

Very low trailing P/E (~4.3x per stockanalysis.com) and conservative balance sheet (gearing ratio 0.02, current ratio 1.87) could offer deep value if the market is overly discounting the FVTPL-driven earnings quality concern

Large, growing securities portfolio (Century Huatong, Moore Threads, and newer AI-chip/compute names) gives optional upside exposure to the broader China AI investment theme, funded by an opportunistic zero-coupon convertible bond rather than dilutive equity
Active capital return (ongoing buybacks, MSCI index inclusion) signals management confidence and improves trading liquidity/visibility
bear_case: Reported FY2025 and H1 2026 'profit' is overwhelmingly a function of unrealized, reversible fair-value gains on listed equity holdings (95% of H1 2026 pre-tax profit) rather than core game-publishing economics; a China/HK equity market correction (particularly in AI-linked names like Moore Threads) could flip reported earnings sharply negative

Core domestic game business is in structural decline: FY2025 revenue down 25.5% YoY, H1 2026 revenue down a further 6.0% YoY, with management explicitly describing legacy IPs as past peak growth and gross billings 'moderating'

The company's own disclosed P&L split (RMB14.2m core operating profit vs RMB268.4m FVTPL gains in H1 2026) means the headline ~4x P/E is materially misleading as a valuation signal on sustainable earnings
Unrelated diversification into pop toys and fast food is a potential distraction/capital-allocation risk with no demonstrated synergy or track record at scale

Small-cap Chinese gaming publisher facing intense competition from much larger, better-capitalized players (Tencent, NetEase, 37 Interactive) for both licensed IP and platform distribution terms, with limited pricing power
Operating cash flow is volatile and driven by working-capital/bills-payable timing rather than a clear trend of cash generation, complicating assessment of true free cash flow
